messages.content:
Design a deterministic online bin-packing heuristic. You are given the current item's size and only feasible existing bins' remaining capacities. Return one score per feasible bin; higher wins and ties choose the first bin. The evaluator opens a new bin only when no existing bin fits. Minimize the number of bins used across the search instances. You cannot see future items.

Return exactly one function: def priority(item, bins):. item is the current positive integer item size; bins is a list of feasible bin residual capacities. Return a numeric list with exactly len(bins) scores, in input order; larger scores are preferred and ties use the earliest bin. The evaluator handles feasibility and opening bins. Use only numeric local assignments, if/else, return, numeric list literals, single-generator list comprehensions over bins or numeric lists, optional comprehension filters, integer list indexing, + - * / // % **, numerical comparisons, and/or/not, and conditional expressions. Permitted calls: abs, min, max, sum, len, round, sqrt, log, exp (no keywords). No imports, attributes, strings, general loops, recursion, external state, list multiplication, generators, or other calls. Do not rebind item, bins, priority, or helper names. Use ASCII-letter-starting names of <=64 characters. All numeric intermediates must be finite with absolute value <=1e12; power requires abs(base)<=1e6 and abs(exponent)<=12; round digits are integers between -12 and 12; exp requires abs(argument)<=100. Source limit 12 KiB, AST limit 1024 nodes/depth 40, list limit 4096, evaluation limit 50000 steps. Language version: funpack-dsl-1.

The following programs and measured search-set bin counts are reference strategies. Lower counts are better. Design one candidate with a coherent decision mechanism that can change which feasible bin is selected relative to the best supplied parent. You may redesign the scoring rule rather than edit its constants. The objective remains fewer bins; novelty alone is not success.
[{"code": "def priority(item, bins):\n    return [1000.0 if r - item == 0 else (-(r - item) + (15 if len(bins) >= 10 and r - item >= 28 and r - item <= 48 else 0) + (10 if r - item >= item and r - item < 3 * item else 0) - (15 if r - item >= 8 and r - item <= 22 else 0)) for r in bins]\n", "counts": [260, 264, 271, 269, 273, 289, 271, 263, 269, 271, 265, 260, 259, 256, 267, 259, 254, 262, 260, 253, 267, 265, 272, 270, 260, 265, 262, 268, 273, 263], "mean_bins": 265.3333333333333}, {"code": "def priority(item, bins):\n    return [1000.0 if r - item == 0 else (-(r - item) + (15 if len(bins) >= 8 and r - item >= 30 and r - item <= 45 else 0) + (10 if r - item >= item and r - item < 3 * item else 0) - (15 if r - item >= 8 and r - item <= 22 else 0)) for r in bins]\n", "counts": [260, 263, 271, 268, 272, 289, 271, 262, 269, 271, 266, 260, 259, 256, 267, 259, 254, 262, 259, 253, 267, 263, 272, 270, 260, 265, 262, 267, 273, 263], "mean_bins": 265.1}]

Choose one mechanism to explore: a piecewise preference over post-placement residuals; a preference depending on the distribution of the currently feasible residual capacities; or a conditional tradeoff between filling tightly and preserving another useful residual size. These are suggestions, not guaranteed improvements. Use only information in item and bins; never assume knowledge of future items or access to unavailable bin state.

For a fixed item, a score that is strictly decreasing in residual capacity will retain Best Fit's ranking. Adding the same item-dependent constant to every score also leaves the ranking unchanged. Avoid proposing such transformations as a new decision mechanism. A rule may agree with Best Fit in many states, but the intended change should have a clear condition under which the ranking can differ. Do not sacrifice feasibility or return an invalid score list.

Start with 'Strategy:' and use at most 80 English words to identify the mechanism, the condition under which the preferred bin may change, and one reason it could help or fail. Treat quality claims as hypotheses. Do not output predicted witness indices or a step-by-step reasoning trace. Then provide one complete priority(item, bins) function in exactly one Python code block using the permitted language. Local execution will measure behavior and packing quality independently of your description.

expect: response JSON object with a 'text' string: Strategy + one python block (enhanced) or one python block only (basic)
